headline: Planning Home Electrical Updates: Costly Mistakes to Avoid Before Hiring a Contractor
articleBody:
When planning a home remodel, electrical updates are easy to overlook until walls are already closed up. Avoiding standard pitfalls saves significant time, money, and hassle during construction.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Adding major appliances without checking panel load: Plugging commercial-grade kitchen appliances into existing circuits can overload your main panel. Always assess capacity first.
- Using mismatched wire gauges and breakers: Putting higher-amp breakers on undersized wire creates an unseen fire risk inside walls.
- Leaving ungrounded or deteriorated wiring hidden: Closing fresh drywall over damaged, brittle, or obsolete wiring forces expensive repairs later.
- Relying on extension cords for permanent equipment: Cords routed behind cabinets or under carpets violate standard safety practices and degrade quickly.
- Neglecting circuit labeling during renovations: Unlabeled panels make future troubleshooting frustrating and slow down routine maintenance.
- Assuming lighting swaps do not affect circuit loads: Adding numerous fixtures or high-output drivers without calculating cumulative amperage leads to unexpected tripping.

What to Prepare Before You Start: Compile a full list of all major appliances, heated floors, and specialty electronics you plan to install so your contractor can map your circuits accurately.
